#### §31: Utilities

| ID | Spec | Ann. | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| D-31.1 | §31 | — | **The utilities are spec §31 with their own decision series D-31 and view `s31` (UTIL-0; `plan/utilities.md` Q7, owner's approval 2026-11-14).** §31 specifies what callers depend on (command names and paths, options, output formats, exit codes, files read and written, environment) for ldconfig, ldd, getent, getconf, iconv, locale, localedef, zic, zdump, tzselect, gencat and pldd, and what is not provided (§31.14); each item cites POSIX, a man page, RFC 8536, Appendix D, or a case of `spec/behaviour/utilities.glibc.txt` (black-box probe `tools/probe/util_spec.sh`, run as an ordinary user on the reference). A behaviour the design decided differently is marked **Liella rule**, with a differences row and a D-31 decision. Tooling: `cargo xtask stubs` reads the sections after §30 (§30, the pattern catalogue, gives no clauses: `spec::NO_CLAUSES`), so §31's clauses are `s31_<sub>_<field>_<n>` and their stubs are `crates/core/tests/s31_utilities_clauses.rs`; `spec/schedule.tsv` gives §31 to the track `UTIL` (from VAL, started 2026-11-14), so each UTIL story specifies its clauses in place. |
| D-31.2 | §31 | — | **Shape of the utilities: a library per domain holding both sides of each file format, one executable per domain, ldconfig freestanding and static (`plan/utilities.md` §3-§4, Q1 and Q2; owner's approval 2026-11-14).** Each format's writer lives in the crate of its reader (the loader cache in `liella-ld`, TZif in a `liella-tz` crate shared with the C library's reader, locales in a `liella-locale` crate, catalogs beside `catopen`'s reader), so reader and writer are tested against each other. `liella-tz` answers as zic, zdump and tzselect and `liella-locale` as locale, localedef, locale-gen, update-locale and validlocale, chosen by `argv[0]`; a domain with one command is a plain program. ldconfig is a freestanding static program with no C library dependency (dpkg needs it before any package operation and while `libc6` is replaced); Liella's `libc-bin` declares interest in the dpkg `ldconfig` trigger. UTIL-SHAPE measures the domain executables against separate programs (start-up instructions, faults, size); a domain that costs more falls back to separate programs (a build change only). Public interfaces: the commands and the file formats; a public Rust `tz` API in `liella-native` after UTIL-10 (UTIL-16); a `locale` API deferred; no new C ABI until a C consumer asks (D-X.10). |
| D-31.3 | §31, App. D | — | **On-disk formats stay compatible (owner's ruling 2026-11-14).** The utilities write TZif per RFC 8536 (zic, §31.9), the loader cache in the Appendix D.3.1 new format with the D.3.2 extensions (ldconfig, §31.2), the locale directory and archive of D.1 (localedef, §31.8), and the catalog format of D.2 (gencat, §31.12), so files written by Liella's tools and by the reference's are interchangeable, and coexistence systems and direct readers keep working. A Liella-native format (for example for the CLDR-derived locale set) is proposed only with a measured gain and a decision of its own. |
| D-31.4 | §31.1, §31.2 | — | **Identity strings of the utilities are Liella's (`plan/utilities.md` Q3; owner's approval 2026-11-14).** The first line of `--version` is `<command> (Liella <version>) 2.39`, the bug-report line of `--help` names Liella's channel, and ldconfig's tag 0 text (`Cache generated by:` in `-p`) names Liella's ldconfig; the trailing ABI level `2.39` stays, so scripts that read the version number see the ABI they get. No compatibility option: the banner states who built the program, and a script that tells C libraries apart (for example by `ldd --version`) must see the truth. The mirror scan of LIELLA-SYSTEM-LIBC-PLAN counts scripts that match the reference's banner text before UTIL-3 ships; a match it finds is raised with the owner. The transcript harness (UTIL-1) masks identity strings when it compares. `getconf GNU_LIBC_VERSION` follows `confstr` (§24), not this decision. |
| D-31.5 | §31.14 | — | **Not installed: `iconvconfig`, `/etc/bindresvport.blacklist`, `sprof`, `sotruss`, `mtrace`, `nscd` (`plan/utilities.md` Q4, owner's approval 2026-11-14; R8).** `iconvconfig` indexes conversion modules and Liella has none (D-6.8: charsets are built in or read from the installed charmaps); `/etc/bindresvport.blacklist` serves Sun RPC, which Liella does not implement; the `libc-devtools` commands have no caller in the caller search of the design; `nscd` is dropped (R8; Liella's name-service cache is in the library, D-16.10). No compatibility option: there is nothing for a restored command to act on. Revisited if the mirror scan of LIELLA-SYSTEM-LIBC-PLAN finds callers. gencat and pldd are kept (UTIL-14, UTIL-15). |
| D-31.6 | §31.2 | — | **`ldconfig -c old` and `-c compat` are refused (`plan/utilities.md` Q5, owner's approval 2026-11-14; #941).** ldconfig prints a message naming the new format as the one it writes and exits nonzero without writing anything; `-c new` (the default) is accepted. No compatibility option: Liella's loader reads only the new format (D-27.16, #941), so an old-format cache would be ignored by the loader it serves. The reference writes the old format on request (probe `ldconfig-c-old`). |
| D-31.7 | §31.3 | SEC | **ldd never runs the operand's code or another interpreter (`plan/utilities.md` Q6, owner's approval 2026-11-14).** ldd lists each operand through Liella's loader in list mode (`--list`, D-27.16), which maps the dependencies and runs none of their code, so ldd and the loader agree on every resolution. For an operand whose `PT_INTERP` is not Liella's loader, ldd lists by Liella's rules and says so on standard error. So ldd on an untrusted file runs none of its code. No compatibility option: running an untrusted file's code is the behaviour this rule exists to remove. `-v` reads the version needs itself. `-d`, `-r` and `-u` need relocation processing, so they are refused with a message until DL-10. |
| D-31.8 | §31.14 | — | **The `locales` commands are Liella's own (`plan/utilities.md` Q8, owner's approval 2026-11-14; R1).** `locale-gen`, `update-locale` and `validlocale` are reimplemented inside `liella-locale` from their man pages (locale-gen(8), update-locale(8)) and the files they use (`/etc/locale.gen`, `/etc/default/locale`, `SUPPORTED`); they compile in process, one parse of each charmap and shared source for all requested locales, in parallel. Counters per locale against one `localedef` process per locale decide any speed claim (UTIL-13). Their interface clauses are added with UTIL-13. |
| D-31.9 | §31.2 | SEC | **ldconfig writes a deterministic cache, replaces it atomically, and treats every file it reads as untrusted (`plan/utilities.md` §4; owner's approval 2026-11-14).** Entries are in the Appendix D.3.3 order, ties broken by configuration order and then path bytes, and directory listings are sorted, so identical trees give byte-identical caches on any file system. The cache is written to a temporary file in its own directory, synced, and renamed over the old one. Every ELF file is bounds-checked and never mapped executable. `-r ROOT` resolves every path inside ROOT with `openat2(RESOLVE_IN_ROOT)` and needs no privilege (the reference also succeeds for an ordinary user, probe `ldconfig-r-user`); `chroot` only where `openat2` is missing. An auxiliary cache (under `/var/cache/ldconfig/`, Liella's own file) only if UTIL-3's counters show a gain. |
| D-31.10 | §31 | — | The utilities' transcript harness (UTIL-1) is `cargo xtask transcript` in xtask/src/transcript/, not scripts under validation/: xtask is std-only with no third-party code, already links liella-ld (whose writer builds a transcript's `cache:` items and whose reader backs the `ldconfig -p` stub until UTIL-3), and its comparator is Rust with unit tests that plants check. Transcripts are data (validation/transcripts/<utility>/*.transcript; format in docs/transcripts.md): argv with argv[0] the bare command name on both sides, the exact environment, stdin, the private root's items, an optional unprivileged user and mount namespace with binds, and the reference's outcome written by `record`. `check` compares Liella with the reference and the reference with the record (a stale record fails); status, stdout, stderr and every written path are compared separately, so text on the wrong stream is a mismatch. Normalisation is only the private root's path (`@ROOT@`) unless a transcript adds a `normalise:` literal with its reason. A host without user namespaces prints SKIPPED with the reason. |
| D-31.11 | §31.2 | — | **ldconfig's engine rules beyond D-31.9 (UTIL-3, `plan/utilities.md` §4; engine `crates/ld/src/ldconfig/`).** (1) A soname link is replaced atomically: a new link under a temporary name in the same directory, renamed over the old one, so a concurrent reader sees the old link or the new one, never none. (2) Directory listings, glob matches and soname groups are sorted before use, so the same tree gives the same messages, links and byte-identical cache on any file system (`listing_order_changes_nothing`, `random_configurations_end_cleanly`). (3) ELF headers are read with bounds-checked positioned reads of the needed bytes only; nothing is mapped. (4) Only ELF files of the native class, byte order and machine are entered in the cache; other ELF files are skipped silently (an open question for multilib systems, raised by UTIL-LDCONFIG-3). (5) An `include` that would re-enter a configuration file already being read (found by file identity), or nest deeper than the engine's depth limit, is refused with one message naming the file and line (`include of <file> would loop (include cycle), ignored`); the rest of the configuration is read as usual and the exit status does not change (`include_cycles_end_with_a_message`). (6) A glibc-hwcaps cache entry whose file name is not its soname stores the key as its own string (the cache writer, `write_hwcaps_key_other_than_the_file_name`). (7) `-l` (link individual libraries) is refused with a message and exit 1 until it is implemented; it is a gap, not a design choice. |
| D-31.12 | §31.2 | — | **The shipped ldconfig is a static PIE with no interpreter, its own start, a bump arena and a system-call file system (UTIL-3, D-31.2, D-31.9).** `cargo xtask so` links `crates/ldconfig-bin` into `target/liella/ldconfig` and refuses it unless it has no `PT_INTERP` and passes the loader's link invariant (L14-1: nothing undefined, no `DT_NEEDED`, only RELATIVE/RELR relocations); it starts as ld.so does (`machine/entry.S` built with `-DLIELLA_LDCONFIG`, the loader's self-relocator), so dpkg can run it while libc6 is replaced and from outside a `--root`. Its allocator is a bump arena over anonymous mappings (the last block grows and shrinks in place; other freed blocks stay until exit): one short-lived, single-threaded process needs no general heap, and the product heap needs a thread block the program does not set up. Its file system (`liella_ld::ldconfig::sysfs`) goes through the kernel `Sys` trait: with `-r ROOT` every path is opened with `openat2(RESOLVE_IN_ROOT)` below a descriptor of ROOT and the last component is acted on through its parent's descriptor, so links, reads and the cache stay inside ROOT with no privilege; a ROOT that cannot be opened makes every operation fail with its error. libc-bin ships it as `/usr/sbin/ldconfig` and runs it on the dpkg `ldconfig` trigger (`-r "$DPKG_ROOT"` when set). Proof: the 12 committed transcripts pass through the binary against the reference (`the_shipped_ldconfig_passes_the_transcripts`); plants `handoff/UTIL-LDCONFIG-4-plants.txt`. |
| D-31.13 | §31.2 | — | **ldconfig links and records the i386 and x32 objects of a multilib x86-64 system with their own type's flags; when one directory holds files of one soname but different types, the highest version wins and its type is recorded, whatever order the directory lists them in (UTIL-3, ruling #5922).** `Arch::LDCONFIG_TYPES` names the ELF types the engine accepts with their cache flags: on x86-64, ELF64 `EM_X86_64` (`0x0303`), ELF32 `EM_386` (`0x0003`) and ELF32 `EM_X86_64` (x32, `0x0803`); any other class, byte order or machine is skipped silently, as before. Probe (`validation/transcripts/ldconfig/foreign-class.transcript`, against the reference): i386 and x32 objects get their soname links and `-v` lines like native ones, cache entries `0x3` and `0x803`, no message. Second probe (same soname, a native and an i386 file in one directory, each case with private roots on ext4 and on tmpfs and in both creation orders): the reference always links the highest version, but its cache flags and its message `libraries <a> and <b> in directory <dir> have same soname but different type.` change with the directory's listing order (an entry can carry the flags of the file the link does not name). That outcome depends on the file system, so it is not a committed transcript. Liella's rule follows §31.2's determinism rule: listings are sorted, the highest version under the D.3.3 comparison wins the link, the entry carries the winner's flags (the type of the file the loader opens through the link), and each other-type file of that soname is reported as `libraries <other> and <winner> in directory <dir> have same soname but different type.`. The link always matches the reference. The message text is the reference's, but the reference printed it only in the listing order where the winner came last, and then its entry carried the loser's flags; Liella prints the message in every order and records the winner's flags, a combination the reference did not show in either order. Test: `foreign_class_objects_are_recorded_with_their_type` (crates/ld/tests/ldconfig.rs, both listing orders). |
| D-31.14 | §31.5 | — | **getconf is a static C front end over Liella's `libc.a`, and its name table is generated from `spec/abi/getconf.tsv` joined with `spec/abi/sysconf.tsv` (UTIL-5, `plan/utilities.md` §4).** `csys/util/getconf.c` is linked by `cargo xtask so` as a static PIE (`liella-rcrt1.o`, `libc.a`) into `target/liella/getconf` and shipped as `/usr/bin/getconf` in libc-bin. Static rather than dynamic: the values are Liella's `sysconf`, `confstr` and `pathconf` in every root and on every build host, with no loader in the way, so the transcripts prove the shipped program itself; it is the same program a dynamic build would be, so a later switch to dynamic (one link line) needs only UTIL-SHAPE's counters. `spec/abi/getconf.tsv` holds the 414 names the reference accepts (320 listed by `-a`, in its order, and 94 accepted but unlisted, such as `TRACE` and `VERSION`), each with the constant it answers from and whether its value prints unsigned (`ULONG_MAX`); the kinds and numbers come from `sysconf.tsv`, the table the library's own answers are generated from (D-24.6), so a name cannot name a constant the library does not have and the build stops if it does. The name set and every behaviour were settled by black-box probes of the reference (candidate names formed from every constant in `sysconf.tsv`); `-v` accepts any specification and does not change a value, as the reference does on x86-64. `GNU_LIBC_VERSION` is `confstr`'s text. `--help` prints the usage paragraph without a bug-reporting address and `--version` prints `getconf (Liella) <version>` (identity strings, plan/utilities.md Q3; no transcript compares them). |

| D-31.17 | §31.7 | — | **The `locale` command is a C front end over the public locale interfaces until UTIL-12 folds it into `niji-locale` (UTIL-8; rulings #6246, #6247).** `csys/util/locale.c` prints keyword values through `nl_langinfo`/`nl_langinfo_l` on their public `<langinfo.h>` items (the keyword table is the reference's 180 keywords, probed with `locale -k LC_<cat>`; value kinds per Appendix D.1.5), lists `-a` from the archive's name table (Appendix D.1.6) and the directories under `/usr/lib/locale` that hold `LC_IDENTIFICATION` plus the built-in `C`, `C.utf8` and `POSIX`, in `strcoll` order, and lists `-m` from `/usr/share/i18n/charmaps`. A `.bz2` charmap is listed by its name only (differences row: nothing installs one). Cost: the program is 206 752 bytes before stripping; the inflater runs only under `-m`, so other start-ups do not change. `time-era-entries` and `category` print exactly the item's own data, its string up to the first NUL byte (ruling #6247: a differences row, no compatibility option). |
| D-31.18 | §31.9 | — | **`zic` makes every file a source names below its output directory, and follows no symbolic link below it (TZ-TOOLS-2; loaded data is untrusted, owner 2026-11-17).** The `-d` directory is the caller's: its path is followed as given and made when missing. Below it, each zone or link name is walked one component at a time from a descriptor of that directory (`mkdirat`, then `openat` with `O_NOFOLLOW`), the file is written under a short private name in its directory and renamed over the name, and a link's old entry is removed with `unlinkat`; a symbolic link anywhere below `-d`, whether this run, an earlier run or someone else made it, is never followed for a write, and a component that is one stops that name with `Can't create directory <name up to it>: Too many levels of symbolic links`. Names are checked as the source is read (empty, leading `/`, a `.`, `..` or empty component, trailing `/`, with the reference's messages, probed), and the walk refuses those components again on its own. A link target that cannot be hard-linked with `EPERM`, such as a directory, is an error (`link from <path> failed`), not a symbolic link (probed). The path length limit applies to the name as resolved from the directory (4095 bytes; probed), and a final component over `NAME_MAX` is refused before anything is removed. Links named by options (`-l`, `-p`, `-t`) are the caller's own paths and are made as given. Rejected: checking resolved paths with `realpath` before each write (a check, then a use: a link made between the two still escapes); following only links that resolve inside `-d` (the same race, and every link must be resolved). |

The program is `crates/localedef-bin` over the boundary feature `localedef` (ldconfig's self-relocator, arena and file layer, its own entry `niji_machine_localedef_entry`), linked by `cargo xtask so` into `target/niji/localedef` with no interpreter and no shared object (D-31.2's checks), so it runs in a build root whatever C library is installed there and needs no allocator over `malloc`. | D-31.20 | §31.8 | — | **`LC_COLLATE`'s weights are libniji's own numbering; the order they give is the reference's, the key bytes are not (UTIL-12, Appendix D.1.4).** A weight is the item's place in one order of collating symbols, characters and elements (wide-character weights are the place + 2); a multibyte weight is the per-level rank of the value written as a prefix-free code: one byte when the level has at most 254 values, otherwise one- and two-byte codes with lead bytes of 2 or more and trail bytes of 1 or more, three bytes past 64770 values. The extra multibyte and wide tables are plain lists (no range entries; `INDIRECT` empty), and the symbol hash items 13 to 15 are empty (size 1, eight zero bytes), since libniji's regex reads no collating-symbol names from them. `crates/locale/tests/reference.rs` checks the order: `strcoll` (multibyte), `wcscoll` and bracket ranges (`collseq`) over a deterministic corpus of 4341 strings for en_US, de_DE, fr_FR, ja_JP and tr_TR UTF-8 and en_US ISO-8859-1 give, for every adjacent pair of the reference's sorted list, the same order under libniji's file (both orders are total preorders, so every pair agrees). No differences row: `strxfrm` keys are specified as comparable with `strcmp`, not as particular bytes, and no program reads `LC_COLLATE`'s bytes but the C library. |

| D-31.22 | §31.8 | — | **localedef's charmaps for the built-in codecs are read off the codecs** (owner ruling #7532: libniji generates its locale data, never from the reference's files). `crates/charmaps` (`niji-charmaps`, a host tool) writes one POSIX charmap (XBD 6.4) for each charset libniji's iconv converts with a built-in codec: ANSI_X3.4-1968, ISO-8859-1, UTF-8, EUC-JP, BIG5, EUC-KR, CP949, GB18030, GBK and WINDOWS-31J (the reference's `locale -m` names for those charsets). It probes the codec through the same `niji::iconv::Conv` iconv runs: every byte sequence it decodes to one character (extending each incomplete prefix up to 4 bytes) is listed when the codec encodes that character back to the same sequence, so each name has one encoding; sequences decoding to a character written another way (CP932's duplicate rows) and encode-only code points are left out, and the header says how many. Runs of consecutive characters on consecutive last bytes are one `<Ua>..<Ub>` line. `<mb_cur_max>` is the longest listed sequence, 6 for UTF-8 (its encoder writes up to 0x7FFFFFFF). WIDTH: the `C.UTF-8` width for UTF-8 and one-byte sequences; in the multi-byte charsets a character of two or more bytes is 2 columns (zero-width ones stay 0), EUC-JP's SS2 half-width katakana and GB18030's four-byte sequences keep their width (with that rule ja_JP.EUC-JP, ja_JP.WINDOWS-31J, ko_KR.EUC-KR and ko_KR.CP949 get the reference's widths exactly; zh_CN.GB18030 still differs in the East Asian ambiguous four-byte characters, which the reference gives 2 columns: the next step needs East Asian Width data); the rule was settled by compiling locales with both localedefs and comparing `wcwidth` (black box). `cargo xtask so` runs the program into `target/niji/locale-charmaps` and gzips each file (`gzip -9n`); the system `locales` package ships them as `/usr/share/i18n/charmaps/<name>.gz`, beside libc6's single-byte charmaps (D-6.16), which are their converters already and are not duplicated (manifest lint). Built-in names are found before any charmap file, so installing these changes no iconv conversion. The other built-in codecs (UTF-16, UTF-32, UCS-2, UCS-4) get none: they are not ASCII-compatible, so no locale can use them; charsets libniji does not convert get none either (the reference's `locale -m` lists 234 names; libniji's now 53). |
| D-31.23 | §31.8 | — | **The tool arena localedef and ldconfig share frees what they free** (#7535). It was a bump arena that gave back only its last block, so a localedef run's peak was the sum of every temporary table (218-338 MB per #14 locale), which matters once locale-gen compiles locales in parallel. Now: requests up to 64 KiB are rounded to a power-of-two class (16 B upwards) and served from 1 MiB chunks, each class with an intrusive free list, so a freed block is reused by the next request of its class; a larger block is its own anonymous mapping, unmapped on free and grown with `mremap`, so the big tables (collation and ctype) give their pages back to the kernel as soon as they are dropped. Peak RSS of `localedef -i <locale> -f UTF-8 <dir>` (Zen 1 host, `/usr/bin/time -f %M`, KiB, base origin/next 8e1837914 -> this change): en_US 224640 -> 109552, de_DE 344160 -> 111576, fr_FR 344160 -> 111560, ja_JP 234240 -> 49936, tr_TR 283680 -> 112540; the output files are unchanged (the reference comparison tests). Chunks are never returned (the small classes' total is a few MB); a size-class allocator was chosen over a general-purpose heap because the tools are single-threaded, short-lived and freestanding (no libc malloc to call). |
| D-31.24 | §31.8 | — | **Superseded by D-31.29.** **localedef writes all twelve category files; a category the source does not define (or, under `-c`, one whose statements failed) gets the POSIX locale's values** (#7534; RELEASE-SNAPSHOT-1122C finding L1: a source of the six POSIX categories gave six files and `setlocale(LC_ALL, ...)` failed). The values come from one built-in source (`crates/locale/src/defaults.rs`) compiled for the run's charmap, so they pass through the same writers as any source. Compared black-box with the reference's files for a one-category source (UTF-8 and ISO-8859-1), they are equal except where the reference's default is not the POSIX locale's value (XBD 7.3), and there libniji keeps POSIX: `LC_CTYPE` gives the ASCII characters their XBD 7.3.1 classes (`print`, `graph`, `cntrl`, `punct`) and widths, and `outdigit`s 0-9 (the reference: none of those classes, width -1, no outdigits); `LC_TIME`'s wide strings and alternative month names are the narrow names (the reference: empty); `LC_MONETARY`'s "not available" numbers are `CHAR_MAX` as `localeconv` of the POSIX locale gives (the reference: 0xff where a source's `-1` gives 0x7f) and `mon_grouping` empty; `LC_ADDRESS`'s `country_ab2`/`country_ab3` are empty (the reference: spaces). Equal: `week 7;19971130;7`, `LC_NUMERIC` grouping empty, the code-point collation, `LC_PAPER` 297x210, `LC_MEASUREMENT` 1, `LC_TELEPHONE`'s `+%c %a%t%l`. A program sees the difference only in a locale built from an incomplete source, where the POSIX values are what the source's author gets from the C locale. Recorded in docs/differences-from-glibc.md; no compat option (a default without classes or widths serves no program); RULING NEEDED on that in the story's hand-back. |
| D-31.25 | §31.8 | — | **localedef writes the locale archive in the Appendix D.1.6 layout, rebuilt whole on every change** (ruling #7533). A NAME without `/` goes into `<prefix>/usr/lib/locale/locale-archive` unless `--no-archive`; `--list-archive`, `--add-to-archive` (with `--replace`) and `--delete-from-archive` change or read it, with the messages and statuses of black-box probes of the reference (spec §31.8). The layout is D.1.6's, not a libniji format, because programs outside libc read it: the reference's `localedef --list-archive` lists a libniji-written archive, and an archive written by either tool is read by libniji's `setlocale` and `locale -a`. Written: the header, a name table (hash, name offset, record offset), the NUL-ended names, the records (a count and 13 (offset, length) slots by category number) and the category images 16-byte aligned, each distinct image stored once (the twelve `LC_MEASUREMENT` files of a dozen locales are often one). The name table is a prime of at least 2n+1 slots, grown until every name's hash has a slot of its own: a reader probing by hash finds a name at its first probe and an absent one at an empty slot, whatever its collision step (the hash, a rotate-by-9-and-add over the bytes seeded with the length, was fitted black-box to the reference's slots for 12 of 12 names; libniji's `setlocale` scans the table and does not depend on it). Unlike the reference the file is not preallocated (3-6.5 MB there): it is exactly the data, and every change writes a new file and renames it over the old one under an `flock` of the locale directory, so a program that has the old archive mapped keeps a consistent image and two localedefs do not lose each other's locales. A deleted name in a reference-written archive keeps its slot with record offset 0; libniji's reader treats that as absent. The archive is untrusted data: the parser checks every offset and length and refuses a damaged file whole (`[error] cannot open locale archive`, status 4) rather than rewriting it. Stored names have the codeset normalized (`niji::locale::name::archive_form`); a NAME without a codeset is stored as given and with the charmap's normalized codeset before any `@modifier` (`en_US` with ISO-8859-1: `en_US` and `en_US.iso88591`), one record for both, as the reference. |
| D-31.26 | §31.8 | — | **localedef reads the source from standard input without `-i`, goes past syntax errors as the reference does, and refuses `--big-endian`** (#7534; statuses and messages from black-box probes of the reference). Standard input is read whole (up to the input limit) and named `<stdin>` in messages. The source parser records a line outside any category (`<file>:<line>: syntax error: not inside a locale definition section`), skips it and goes on; the locale is written with or without `-c`, status 1. A category whose statements fail is reported as `<file>:<line>: <CATEGORY>: syntax error: <what>` (the reference stops after `syntax error`; libniji says what was wrong) and gets its default (D-31.24); without `-c` that is status 4 and no output (`[error] no output file produced because errors were issued`), with `-c` the locale is written, status 1. An error that leaves the source unreadable as a whole (a category without `END`, a `copy` that cannot be resolved) still stops the compile, status 4. `--big-endian` is refused (`[error] big-endian output is not supported`, status 4): libniji currently supports only little-endian x86-64 (a design that does not exclude big-endian targets; the writer's byte order is fixed at about 30 sites across the category, collation and archive builders, so choosing it at output is roadmap work) and no libniji program reads big-endian locale files yet, so writing them would be untested output for no reader; the reference writes them, status 0. Recorded in docs/differences-from-glibc.md; RULING NEEDED in the story's hand-back on whether a compat option is wanted (recommended: no). |
| D-31.27 | §31.8 | — | **The locale sources are generated from Unicode CLDR, never taken from the reference's files** (owner ruling #7532; coordinator ruling #7767 on the names CLDR lacks). Data: CLDR 49 (`https://unicode.org/Public/cldr/49/cldr-common-49.zip`, SHA-256 `78403d8d6fb1fed6e208bf9001bf5be00bb5abfd9f8110dae062bf49309d6a89`), Unicode License v3 (`spec/cldr/49/LICENSE`). **Vendored subset, not a build-time fetch:** `tools/cldr/cldr_extract.py` (run by hand when the pin changes; it downloads the archive or takes a copy, refuses any other SHA-256, reads it in place) writes `spec/cldr/49/locales.tsv` (per locale name, the CLDR values its source is made from, resolved through CLDR's parent locales, root and aliases), `territories.tsv` (currency and its digits, paper size, measurement system, first day of the week, weekend end, minimal days of week 1, ISO 3166 codes), `allkeys_CLDR.txt` (CLDR's root collation) and `LICENSE`; the build reads only these (2.3 MB of collation data, 1 MB of values). `--check` fails when an output would change. **Names:** `spec/cldr/locale-names.tsv`, the names the reference's locales package offers (509 SUPPORTED entries, 350 source names); a name is generated when CLDR has its locale, its language with a script the modifier selects (`@latin`, `@cyrillic`, `@devanagari`, `@iqtelif`, `@valencia`), or its language (eu_FR: Basque strings, France's territory data). 65 names (62 base locales) have no CLDR language data and are not generated: a guessed language would be a silent wrong result, a missing locale fails cleanly in `setlocale` (differences row). **Generator:** `xtask/src/locales.rs` (`cargo xtask locale-sources <dir>`): CLDR date and time patterns become `strftime` formats with padded numeric fields (`d_fmt` from the `yMd` skeleton with a 4-digit year; `t_fmt` `%r` for 12-hour locales; `t_fmt_ampm` from `hms`; `d_t_fmt` the medium date-time combination of `yMMMEd` and `t_fmt`; `date_fmt` that plus `%Z`); `grouping` and `mon_grouping` from the number patterns; currency placement and spacing from the currency pattern; `yesexpr`/`noexpr` from CLDR's `posix` messages, adding ASCII y/n where the other answer does not use the letter; week data, paper and measurement from the territory. `LC_CTYPE` copies `i18n`, which copies `i18n_ctype`, written from the derivation the built-in `C.UTF-8` uses (`spec/unicode/15.1.0`, D-5.4: classes, `combining`, `combining_level3`, simple case maps); tr and az add SpecialCasing.txt's dotted/dotless i mappings. `LC_COLLATE` copies `iso14651_t1`, CLDR's root collation as collating symbols per distinct weight of each level, every listed character and contraction, then the code points UTS #10 10.1.3 weights implicitly (Tangut, Nushu, Khitan, core Han, other Han: Unified_Ideograph and the blocks from `spec/unicode/15.1.0`), each its own primary in code point order, as `..` ranges; unassigned code points share the undefined element, which sorts first. **Variable weighting "shifted" (UTS #10 section 4), not CLDR root's default non-ignorable:** the elements CLDR marks variable (spaces and punctuation, `*`), and a level-1-ignorable element after one, are ignorable at levels 1 to 3 and keep their place at level 4; so `a-b`, `a b` and `ab` sort together and `.hidden` sorts among the h words, the order `sort` and `ls` users of the C library have (measured black box: strcoll of a 68-string corpus equals the reference's in en_US, de_DE, fr_FR, it_IT, pt_BR, ru_RU and nl_NL; non-ignorable put every punctuated string before the digits). CLDR's per-language tailorings (`common/collation/<lang>.xml`) are not yet applied: ja, tr, sv, es, pl, zh and ko order by the root (differences row). `LC_CTYPE` adds `translit_combining` (each canonical full decomposition with the combining marks, General_Category M*, removed: é to e) and `translit_compat` (each compatibility decomposition, marks removed: ﬁ to fi, ² to 2), both from UnicodeData.txt. **The source `C` (`localedef -i C -f UTF-8` gives `C.UTF-8`; LOCALE-C-UTF8-SOURCE) is libniji's own, not CLDR's:** `LC_CTYPE` copies `i18n` (the built-in `C.UTF-8`'s classes and simple case maps), `LC_COLLATE` is every code point in code point order as one run of equal-width names (`<U00000000>` `..` `<U0010FFFF>`; the reference's localedef refuses `<U0000>..<U10FFFF>`), which localedef writes as the compact no-rules table (D-31.31), and the other categories hold the POSIX locale's values (POSIX.1-2024 XBD 7.3; paper A4, metric). `SUPPORTED` lists `C.UTF-8 UTF-8` in the name list's order. Checked in `crates/locale/tests/reference.rs` (`generated_c_source_compiles_to_the_builtin_c_utf8`): compiled for UTF-8, every code point has the built-in's classes, case maps and width and `LC_COLLATE` is the code point order. **Packaging:** `cargo xtask so` writes the tree afresh to `target/niji/locale-sources`; the system `locales` package ships each file at `/usr/share/i18n/locales/<name>` and `SUPPORTED` at `/usr/share/i18n/SUPPORTED` (one manifest row each; `manifest.py lint --products` refuses a generated file without a row), and `tools/deb/copyright` carries a `Files:` paragraph for them with the Unicode License v3 text. Every character other than ASCII letters, digits and space is written as `<Uxxxx>`, so the sources need no charmap names beyond those. Data CLDR does not have (postal formats, telephone codes, vehicle codes, name formats) is left out of `LC_ADDRESS`, `LC_TELEPHONE` and `LC_NAME` rather than invented. |
| D-31.28 | §31.12, App. D.2.2 | — | **`gencat` is a C program in `csys/util`, linked dynamically against `libc.so.6` like `getent`, and its catalogs are byte-identical to the reference's for the same source (UTIL-14, GitHub issue #12).** The writer is small and self-contained (parse, merge with an existing catalog, plane search, pool, `-H` header), so it follows the `zic` precedent rather than a Rust library per domain: nothing else reads or writes the source format. Byte identity makes catalogs built either way interchangeable; every rule the spec and POSIX leave open was settled by black-box transcripts of the reference's program (`validation/transcripts/gencat/`): the plane size runs up from n/5+1 while it can still beat the best P*D (a tie goes to the larger P); the pool holds the sets in the reverse of the order they were first named, the default set 1 counting as named first, and each set's messages in ascending signed 32-bit order; a symbolic set or message takes the next number after the signed maximum (from 0) of the sets named by `$set` lines or of the set's messages; without `--new` the existing catalog's messages are added after the sources for keys the sources do not define. |
| D-31.29 | §31.8 | — | **localedef writes all twelve category files; a category the source does not define (or, under `-c`, one whose statements failed) gets the reference's defaults** (#7534; RELEASE-SNAPSHOT-1122C finding L1: a source of the six POSIX categories gave six files and `setlocale(LC_ALL, ...)` failed). Supersedes D-31.24 (which wrote the POSIX locale's values). Settled by the three-way rule (ruling #7754, LOCALEDEF-INPUTS): POSIX.1-2017 XBD 7.3 says a locale definition file holds "one or more" category definitions and "In the event that some of the information for a locale category ... is missing from the locale source definition, the behavior of that category, if it is referenced, is unspecified"; the localedef utility page (XCU) and localedef(1)/locale(5) say nothing more, so the values are the implementation's and libniji writes the reference's, settled black box: `crates/locale/tests/reference.rs` `undefined_categories_get_the_references_defaults` compares every item of every file with the reference's for a one-category source (UTF-8 and ISO-8859-1), none excepted, and five per-category tests check the values without the reference. The values: `LC_CTYPE`'s ASCII letters and digits in `alpha`/`upper`/`lower`/`digit`/`xdigit`/`print`/`graph`, white space in `space`/`blank` (space also `print`), punctuation and controls in no class and width -1, no wide input digits; `LC_TIME`'s English names and formats, wide forms empty up to `t_fmt`, alternative month names empty; `LC_MONETARY`'s "not available" numbers 0xff, `mon_grouping` the one byte 0x7f, CRNCYSTR `-`; `LC_ADDRESS`'s country codes of spaces; `LC_NUMERIC` `.` without grouping, `week 7;19971130;7`, the code-point collation, `LC_PAPER` 297x210, `LC_MEASUREMENT` 1, `LC_TELEPHONE`'s `+%c %a%t%l`. One built-in source (`crates/locale/src/defaults.rs`) compiled for the run's charmap through the same writers as any source; the four items a source cannot state (the empty wide `LC_TIME` strings, no wide input digits, the unterminated `mon_grouping`, CRNCYSTR) the writers give when told they compile the defaults. No differences row (replaces the earlier POSIX-locale values and their row). |
| D-31.30 | §31.8 | — | **Locale data Unicode CLDR has no source for comes from black-box probes of the reference's compiled locales** (owner ruling #7791; extends D-31.27). **Probe:** `tools/probe/locale_dump.py`, run on a system with the reference's compiled locales installed (libc6 2.39-0ubuntu8.9, locales-all 2.39-0ubuntu8.12; 511 names in `locale -a`), runs the reference's own `locale charmap` and `locale -ck` for LC_TELEPHONE, LC_ADDRESS, LC_NAME, LC_PAPER, LC_MEASUREMENT, LC_IDENTIFICATION, LC_NUMERIC, LC_MONETARY, LC_TIME and LC_MESSAGES and writes `spec/locale-probe/locales.tsv` (one row per keyword, the printed bytes with every byte outside printable ASCII and the backslash as `\xHH`, the codeset per name; a non-UTF-8 name keeps only the rows whose text differs from its UTF-8 sibling's, checked by decoding both). `time-era-entries` is left out (not a text item; `era` carries the entries). `tools/probe/locale_fingerprint.c` (through `--fingerprints`) writes `spec/locale-probe/fingerprints.tsv`: per UTF-8 name, FNV-1a hashes of every POSIX class, `towupper`, `towlower` and `wcwidth` over all code points, and of the `wcscoll` order of 13 script-group corpora. **Generator:** `LC_NAME`, `LC_ADDRESS` and `LC_TELEPHONE` of every generated locale are the probe's values (the reference's wins over CLDR's territory and language names for parity; the cross-check against CLDR's ISO 3166 codes and names is in the story's report), and the 65 names CLDR does not cover, with `eo`, `syr` and `tok` (no territory), are generated from the probe in every category above (349 of the 350 source names are generated; `C` waits, D-31.27). `LC_CTYPE` and `LC_COLLATE` cannot be dumped: every generated name takes en_US's (`copy "i18n"`, root order) plus the code points the probe found its classes add and its own case pairs (`locale_fingerprint --diff en_US.utf8`, through `locale_dump.py --ctype-diff`, writes `spec/locale-probe/ctype-diff.tsv`: over all 327 UTF-8 names only U+1361 ETHIOPIC WORDSPACE in `space` for sixteen Ethiopic names and dotted/dotless i for az_AZ, crh_UA, ku_TR, tr_CY, tr_TR and tt_RU@iqtelif, #7892); a difference an addition cannot express (a code point taken out of a class, or a fingerprint difference the diff does not list) is a gap written in the source's comment (none today); a name the probe lacks keeps SpecialCasing.txt's tr / az pairs. Verified: every generated locale compiled by libniji's localedef and read back by the reference's `locale -k` (LOCPATH) equals the probe in all LC_NAME, LC_ADDRESS and LC_TELEPHONE keywords (349 names); the probe-generated names equal it in every probed category except LC_IDENTIFICATION. No locale source file of the reference was viewed (the ruling's narrow exception was not needed). |
| D-31.31 | §31.8 | — | **localedef writes a code point order as an `LC_COLLATE` without rules, and keeps a `..` run as one item until a line names a character inside it** (LOCALE-SOURCES-GEN #7792: the C.UTF-8 source, all of Unicode as one `..` run, took 31 MB of `LC_COLLATE` and 1.2 GB of memory). An order is plain code point order when every character of the charmap is placed in increasing code point order (by `..` runs or line by line), each weighted by itself at every level, with no collating element, no `UNDEFINED` line and a forward first level, and the charmap's byte order is its code point order (so `strcoll`, which compares bytes without rules, and `wcscoll`, which compares code points, agree with the order). Such an order is written as the reference's own compiled C.UTF-8 is (probed: 1406 bytes, `_NL_COLLATE_NRULES` 0, the collating-symbol hash size word 0, the collation-sequence values of the 256 bytes and of the first 256 code points, the codeset name), item for item (the code point table by value). Any other order keeps the tables; a run is placed character by character the moment a line names one of its characters (an order line or `reorder-after`), and all remaining runs before the tables are written, so the file of such an order is the one the eager form gave. Measured (Zen 1 host): the C.UTF-8 order (`<U00000000>`, `..`, `<U0010FFFF>`) compiles to 1530 bytes with 5 MB peak RSS (the eager form: 31 MB and 1.2 GB, LOCALE-SOURCES-GEN); the reference's `strcoll`, `wcscoll`, `strxfrm` and `wcsxfrm` on that file give its installed C.UTF-8's results on every pair of 60 code points over every plane (surrogates excluded). The reference's localedef compiles the same source to tables (7.2 MB, 177 MB of memory, probed) whose order differs from its C.UTF-8's on 2850 of those 3600 pairs: a differences row, without a compat option (ruling #7942: a source wanting the tables adds any weight that is not the character itself). An `LC_COLLATE` section without an `order_start` (empty, or `collating-symbol` lines only) is refused as the reference refuses it (probe `localedef-empty-collate`, spec §31.8 Failure): `<file>:<END line>: LC_COLLATE: empty category description not allowed`, `[error] too many errors; giving up`, status 1 with or without `-c`, no category file written; the 88-byte file libniji wrote before had no rules and no hash size word, and the reference's `setlocale` refused it. The default `LC_COLLATE` (a category the source does not define, D-31.29) is the reference's 92-byte file, item for item. |
| D-31.32 | §31.8 | — | **The shared root of the generated `LC_COLLATE` is generated from the DUCET (`spec/unicode/15.1.0/allkeys.txt`, UTS #10) plus a 228-line rules file (`spec/locale/collate-root.txt`), not committed as a probed table** (coordinator decision #7958, recommended by LOCALE-COLLATE-TAILORINGS; owner ruling #7791: locale data by black-box probe). `crates/collate-root` (niji-collate-root) writes the root as a locale source. Levels 1-3 are the DUCET's weights with variable weighting "shifted" (UTS #10 section 4); Han code points the DUCET does not list take the implicit weights of UTS #10 section 10.1; level 4 is the character itself, and characters equal at levels 1-3 are in code point order. One probe of the reference's en_US.UTF-8 over U+0001-U+10FFFF settled this tie-break: listing the reference's order with these weights gives the reference's level for all adjacent pairs but 45 of 50,708. What the model does not give is a rule in the rules file, and each rule carries its probe evidence (#7958 condition 3): two class rules (`han-variant-block`: 1,508 CJK radical, compatibility and enclosed ideographs form one block before U+4E00; `format-first`: the 467 Cc/Cf/Variation_Selector code points with all-zero DUCET weights come first at level 4), 127 undefined ranges (only U+4E00-U+9FA5 of the unified ideographs are defined), 33 `after` placements, 1 `same`, 3 `expand` and 2 `contract` (l·, L·). `tools/probe/collate/root_rules.py` derives the file from the probe output (results/locale-collate-2026-11-23.md section 7). The proof is equality with the reference on a host with all locales (#7958 condition 2): `generated_root_collation_is_the_references_en_us` compiles the root with libniji's localedef library and checks all 1,112,063 code points for the reference's `strxfrm` order and every adjacent pair for the reference's level, then checks the corpus with `strcoll` and `wcscoll`. Gain over committing the probed 120k-line table: the data is traceable to the spec and compact, and a DUCET update becomes a regeneration. Not decided here: the per-locale tailorings and their wiring into the generated locale sources (a later story stacked on the locale-source generator); bracket-range collation sequence order (collseq), which differs from the reference and is reported by the test without being asserted; root contractions beyond l·/L·, which are not probed. |
| D-31.33 | §31.8 | — | **The generated locale sources carry one probed transliteration table, `translit_shared`, which every generated `LC_CTYPE` includes** (owner ruling #7791; extends D-31.30; follow-up #7957 of LOCALEDEF-TRANSLIT). **Probe:** `tools/probe/translit_probe.c` runs the reference's `iconv` with `<codeset>//TRANSLIT` on every code point 1..0x10FFFF the codeset lacks, under each of the reference's 182 legacy-codeset locales (and en_US.utf8 for ASCII); `tools/probe/translit_table.py` writes `spec/locale-probe/translit.tsv`. A locale's `default_missing` (the result for U+E000, a private-use code point no table names: `?` in most, empty in ku_TR, tr_CY and tr_TR) is left out, since an entry giving it cannot be told apart from no entry. **Rule:** a code point is in the shared table when most locales lacking it give a result (2,419 entries); its alternatives are ordered so that each codeset's own result is the first the codeset can hold. A locale whose own strings hold a code point its result treats otherwise gets an entry of its own before the include (ro_RO: U+021B to U+0163; uz_UZ: U+02BB, U+0419, U+0439, U+04B2, U+04B3). **Generator:** `xtask/src/locales.rs` emits `translit_shared` and, in each `LC_CTYPE`, the own entries, then `include "translit_shared";""`, then the combining and compatibility includes; `xtask/src/locale_probe.rs` reads a legacy name's value as its UTF-8 sibling's text when the table explains the difference (so the `@euro` wide thousands separators keep U+202F in the source and compile to the reference's bytes). **Verified:** every legacy `SUPPORTED` entry compiled by libniji's localedef in its own codeset against the probe's own rows: 394 values in 86 of the 182 entries, the 251 values in 81 entries LOCALE-PROBE-GEN-2 measured included, and the wide thousands separators of those entries (560 values in all), 0 differ (`crates/locale/tests/reference.rs`). **Remaining:** run-time `iconv //TRANSLIT` in a generated locale differs from the reference's in 38,814 (locale, code point) pairs in 104 of 183 locales, where those locales have tables of their own beyond the shared one (ko_KR.euckr 10,416, ja_JP.eucjp 4,478, zh_* about 1,500 to 2,100 each, tr_* and ku_TR 1,854, uk_UA 585, el_* 493, ar_* 133); compiled values are unaffected. No locale source file of the reference was viewed. |
| D-31.34 | §31.11 | — | **tzselect is a C front end beside zic and zdump (`csys/util/tzselect.c`, dynamic, libc only); its `-c` list is in increasing great-circle distance, and `-n` takes a positive number only** (GitHub #14). Prompts, menus, menu layout, accepted answers, country order, transliteration, the information block, accepted TZ strings and exit statuses come from black-box transcripts of the reference (handoff/UTIL-TZSELECT-PLDD.md); the zone tables are `iso3166.tab` and `zone1970.tab` of `$TZDIR` (default `/usr/share/zoneinfo`), the two the reference was probed to need. **`-c` order:** tzselect(1) promises the zones "roughly in increasing order of distance"; the reference's order was not reproduced by the haversine, law-of-cosines, chord, weighted Euclidean or L1 metrics, in degrees or radians, nor by misreadings of DDMM as decimal degrees, so libniji orders by the haversine of the central angle (monotone in the great-circle distance, computed with a 13-term sine series so the program needs no libm), ties in table order: the list holds the same zones as the reference's when LIMIT covers them all, in an order a user can check. **`-n`:** a LIMIT that is not a positive decimal number is a usage error (`-n <v>: LIMIT must be a positive number`, status 1). **Missing tables:** the message names the file without a script line number. No compat option for these: the reference's `-c` order follows no documented rule to restore, and its results for a non-numeric or zero LIMIT and its line number carry no information a caller can use (differences rows "tzselect -c order", "tzselect -n", "tzselect without its tables"). The `-c` labels name each country by its `iso3166.tab` name except the code `US`, which stays as is (probed). End of input at any prompt exits 1 (s31_11_f_1), after a newline on standard output when it came at a menu (probed). |
| D-31.35 | §31.13 | — | **pldd reads the debugger rendezvous of a stopped target through `/proc/PID/mem`** (GitHub #14; `csys/util/pldd.c`, dynamic, libc only). Weighed: (a) `/proc/PID/maps` lists mapped files, not loaded objects: it misses the vDSO's name, shows realpaths instead of the names the loader recorded, and lists any file the program mapped itself; (b) `dl_iterate_phdr` runs only inside the process; (c) the rendezvous (`DT_DEBUG` of the program's `PT_DYNAMIC` holds the address of `struct r_debug`, `<link.h>`, whose `r_map` starts the `link_map` list; the System V ABI and every debugger use it) gives exactly the objects the loader has, dlopen'd ones included, in load order, with their recorded names. Chosen: (c). Steps: `PTRACE_SEIZE` and `PTRACE_INTERRUPT` every task of `/proc/PID/task` (rescanned until a scan finds no new task), which applies the kernel's tracing permission (Yama's `ptrace_scope` included; refused: `cannot attach to process <pid>: <strerror>`, status 1) and stops the loader from changing the list while it is read; `AT_PHDR`/`AT_PHNUM` from `/proc/PID/auxv`; the load bias from `PT_PHDR` (else `AT_ENTRY` less the program's `e_entry`); `DT_DEBUG`; the list after its first entry (the program) printed by `l_name`; every task detached with the signal it was stopped with, if any. The pointer size follows the program's ELF class. The target's memory is untrusted: each read can fail and ends the walk, at most 65536 entries are printed and a name is cut at `PATH_MAX` bytes, so a corrupt or cyclic list cannot hang or crash pldd. A process without the rendezvous (a static program) prints nothing, status 1, as the reference (probed). Options, messages and statuses as probed (s31_13_*); `--help` without the bug-report lines and `-V` in the house form (D-31.4). |
| D-31.36 | §31.14 | — | **`locale-gen`, `update-locale` and `validlocale` are commands of the shipped `localedef`, chosen by `argv[0]`** (`crates/locale/src/cmds.rs`, dispatch in `crates/boundary/src/localedef.rs`; plan/utilities.md §2 and §4). The `locales` package installs `/usr/sbin/{locale-gen,update-locale,validlocale}` as links to `../bin/localedef`. Weighed: (a) shell scripts calling `localedef` once per locale, the reference's shape: each call parses its charmap and the shared sources again and needs a shell and `sed` in the root; (b) one program per command: three copies of the same static code; (c) commands of `localedef` (chosen): `locale-gen` compiles every selected locale in one process through the `localedef` command itself (`prog::run`, its messages and statuses unchanged), and a root with no shell can still run them (`dpkg --root` configures the libniji-only root through them). `locale-gen` (locale-gen(8), locale.gen(5), black-box probes of the reference's `locales` 2.41 in a trixie root; transcripts in the story's handoff): reads `/etc/locale.gen`; a line is an entry unless it is blank or its first non-blank byte is `#`; an entry is `<locale> <charset>`, compiled from the source named by the locale without its codeset (`ca_ES@valencia` for `ca_ES.UTF-8@valencia`) with the charmap `<charset>`, stored under the locale as written; an entry without a charset prints `error: Bad entry '<locale> '` and is skipped. Output: `Generating locales (this might take a while)...`, one `  <locale-without-codeset>.<charset><@modifier>... done` per compiled entry (localedef's own messages in between), `Generation complete.`; status 0, as probed, also for an unknown option, an operand or a failed locale. Without `--keep-existing` the archive `/usr/lib/locale/locale-archive` is removed first and rebuilt with exactly the selected locales (the reference's default form on trixie is the archive); with it, an entry the archive already holds is skipped. A missing `/etc/locale.gen` is a silent success that leaves the archive alone (probed). Any other read error: `locale-gen: cannot read /etc/locale.gen: <strerror>`, status 1. |
| D-31.37 | §31.14 | — | **`update-locale`, `validlocale` and the `locales` package's maintainer scripts** (update-locale(8), validlocale(8), debconf-devel(7); black-box probes of the reference's `locales` 2.41 in a trixie root; commands of `localedef`, D-31.36). `update-locale [--help] [--reset] [--locale-file FILE \| --locale-file=FILE] [--no-checks] [NAME=value \| NAME]...` edits `/etc/locale.conf` (the postinst links `/etc/default/locale` to `../locale.conf`, as the reference's trixie package does) in place: a `NAME=value` operand replaces the line of that variable, commented (`#NAME=`) or not, else is appended in operand order; a bare `NAME` comments its line out; `--reset` first comments out every active variable no operand names; an empty line is written back as `#` (trixie's `locales` 2.41; Ubuntu 24.04's 2.39 keeps it empty: a distribution difference, libniji follows the Debian suite it ships for); a missing or empty file starts with the line `#  File generated by update-locale`. Then, unless `--no-checks` (both checks are skipped, probed on both references): every active `LANG` and `LC_*` value must be available (as `validlocale` decides), else `*** update-locale: Error: invalid locale settings: ` and the active settings, status 255, the file unchanged, `LANGUAGE` unwarned; after that a `LANGUAGE` whose first language differs from `LC_ALL`'s (else `LANG`'s) language, unless that is `C` or `POSIX` (`C.UTF-8` is not exempt), is commented out with `*** update-locale: Warning: LANGUAGE (<v>) is not compatible with <NAME> (<v>). Disabling it.` on standard output. An unknown option prints `Unknown option: <name>` on standard error and is ignored; `--help` prints the usage on standard error, status 0. `validlocale LOCALE`: available (the empty name, `C`, `POSIX`, `C.UTF-8` in any codeset spelling, a name the archive holds in its stored or written form, or a `/usr/lib/locale/<name>/LC_CTYPE`): `locale '<name>' valid and available` on standard error, status 0. Else the `/etc/locale.gen` line to add on standard output, `<name> <charset>` with the charset of its `SUPPORTED` entry, or `$DEFAULTCHARSET`, or `ISO-8859-1`, then `locale '<name>' not available` on standard error, status 1. No operand: `Usage: <program> <locale>` on standard output, status 1, the program named as a shell names a script: argv[0] when it holds a `/`, else the first `PATH` directory holding it joined to it (probed: a bare `validlocale` prints `/usr/sbin/validlocale`). Package (tools/deb/system/locales.*): debconf questions `locales/locales_to_be_generated` (multiselect over `SUPPORTED`) and `locales/default_environment_locale`; the postinst creates `/etc/locale.gen` once (every `SUPPORTED` entry commented out; the administrator's file from then on, not a conffile), rewrites it under debconf so that exactly the chosen entries are selected (a chosen entry's line uncommented, any other selected line commented out with `# `, a chosen entry the file lacks appended, every `SUPPORTED` entry the file lacks appended commented out), runs `locale-gen`, then sets or clears `LANG` with `update-locale`. It honours `DPKG_ROOT` and runs the root's static commands through chroot, so `dpkg --root` configures a root with only libniji's packages and no shell; under `DPKG_ROOT` or without debconf it asks nothing and compiles `/etc/locale.gen` as it is. `/etc/locale.alias` ships with comments only (no aliases: the reference's alias list is its own data). |
